utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Karnavas, before we have the next witness, is there anything that you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, there are two matters, Your Honour. One is today we received some disclosure material that dates back to incident from May 25, 1995. It's exculpatory in a sense because it validates our position that the strikes on May 25, 1995 were as a result of the NATO bombings that occurred in Pale. And of course, this is -- this issue was raised when Witness Mico Gavric was here. The Prosecution was able to locate a document with respect to some strikes on that day. We were able to find the NIAD report which indicated their opinion as to why the strikes occurred. And now we have documents from the Muslim army giving their assessment. Obviously, they're exculpatory, we believe, because it at least demonstrates the reasons why that occurrence took place, the justification, if there is such a thing, for that. But more importantly, why it's not part of some overall joint criminal enterprise, at least pursuant to the theory of the Prosecution that would have commenced sometime in June 1995. My complaint is, if we can term it that way, is that I understand we have a lot of documents. The Prosecution has a lot of search engines. I bring a witness here. I anticipate the best I can. I would expect the Prosecution to by now since they have our witness list to begin to do early searches, and I really appreciate and admire their efforts to bring these documents at this late of the day. However, it does prejudice me somewhat in that now I have no opportunity to at least show these documents to the gentleman to at least point that there is -- there are alternative reasons other than perhaps the ones that the trial -- the Prosecution would want to argue. So now I have to find a way to get these documents in. The reason I'm making -- I'm asking for this little meeting is to please instruct the Prosecution to make any additional efforts they can, now that they know our witness list, to try to locate any documents that they might have. We understand they're doing that. But we would appreciate if perhaps they could do it all the witnesses and not wait until the last moment because it's causing a lot of grieve. That's the first issue. The second issue, and perhaps we can deal with even after the -- today's hearing because I think the witnesses will be rather short. Last week in the Institute of War and Peace Reporting, a report came out where it states that Milan Lukic of Visegrad had been cooperating with the OTP investigators in order -- in giving them information, potential information with respect to Karadzic. Now, of course I'm sceptical of the media, as most people are. But however, it would appear at least from reading this, it says that the Tribunal would not confirm that Milan Lukic had arranged a meeting, but they told IWPR team that he was in regular contact with them, in other words with the Office of the Prosecution or investigators from the office of the Prosecution. We believe that this is exculpatory information. We would like to know, and perhaps Mr. McCloskey is unaware of these efforts, but we would like the Trial Chamber to instruct the Prosecution to get to the bottom of this and tell us whether they are contacting Lukic, whether they have information from Lukic, whether they -- we can arrange a meeting with Mr. Lukic to take his deposition and so on and so forth. But I think this might be exculpatory information, particularly since the Prosecution would have its cake and it's eating it, too. On the one hand, they're claiming that Lukic was involved; on the other hand, they're negotiating for him to give them information about Karadzic. And, of course, from my experience negotiating with criminals in the past only tends to bring out the worst of evidence from them as we have seen with Mr. Nikolic and Mr. Deronjic. So those are the things I wanted to bring to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Dealing with that second issue first, I've heard similar press reports. I have no reason to believe any of that is true. Milan Lukic is an indicted war criminal of some of the most vicious crimes imaginable, and I have no reason to believe any of that's true. And if I get any information on that, that is of a discoverable nature I will share it. And of course, Mr. Karnavas knows he can come to me and discuss this sort of thing with me, and I will search and look and ask questions and find if it's there. So I don't know why that kind of thing is necessary to talk about in open court. Regarding the first issue, complaining that you're getting discovery is a new one for me. And as the could you recall recalls, Mico Gavric got up and made this statement that they never fired a shot at the enclave until July 11th. That piqued our interest, so we looked into it. The Court saw what we found, these May 25th documents that we were able to get quickly for the Court that we, of course, provided. We've continued to look at that. We think this is a very significant incident. And it does appear as if it was retaliation for NATO bombing. But retaliation for NATO bombing by striking a civilian target is a war crime, a serious war crime. This is the same day that another corps fired artillery rounds into Tuzla killing 70 kids, civilians, in the downtown of Tuzla, clearly an organised effort by the VRS to strike back at civilian targets to try to dissuade NATO from attacking them. In this case, it's extremely important, it shows the first day of Mr. Blagojevic's day in office. He is going along with the corps orders to fire serious heavy artillery rounds right in downtown Srebrenica, and you will hear more on this evidence because there were casualties, and I won't argue anything more on it. But this was a very nasty incident. It shows -- it gets into the intent of the people involved. And so we fully intend to search this out. And as we get material, as is our agreement, we'll provide that to Mr. Karnavas. I don't see anything exculpatory in this, that his client is involved in war crimes. So I will continue to provide that information, and we will continue to -- to try to find as much as we can on this incident, and we will be asking witnesses about it as is appropriate and is relevant. So that would be my response to the first issue brought up by Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's very difficult for the Bench to make a ruling at this stage because we haven't received the document yet. We don't know the contents of it. But one matter I would like to bring attention to is that I think we should beware of the proliferation of this case. We should concentrate on the incidents after July 11th. If we reach back, well, we should go a long way back, and at this stage I would not like to see we make the case bigger and bigger. So this Trial Chamber only admits the documents which is closely relevant to this particular case. As for the Srebrenica incidents, I think it's a big, very big issue. This Tribunal might have another opportunity to deal with it in the future or some historians will make some comments on it. I believe that's their job. Our job is to see whether the two accused are guilty or not. I think this is all I have to say at this stage because we almost have no information about this document at this moment. But we encourage the parties to get in touch with the other to solve any problems facing them, and as the last resort, the Chamber will do its best to assist the parties for the smooth sailing of the proceedings. Mr. Karnavas, are you ready for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Milomir Tanasijevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: T-a-n-a-s-i-j-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Mr. Tanasijevic, could you please tell us where are you from?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you go to school?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica where I completed elementary school, and I completed secondary school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you do your JNA training?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where it was that you did your training.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In what unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Tito's Guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In what year was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, after you completed your military service, where did you work?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I worked until 1980 in the Vares factory in Potocari. And in 1980, I move to the lead and zinc mine of Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I worked in maintenance, the maintenance for pit machinery and mining machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have any particular training?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what training did you receive?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Higher education, and I received training, and later on in Belgrade I went on to grade 5 for the mechanical engineering stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, sir, are you currently employed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where do you currently live?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I live in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in 1992 when the war broke out, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you stay in Srebrenica throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: To Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why did you leave Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Because the Muslims killed three members of my immediate family in an ambush. They were unarmed, and we saw that we would all lose our lives like that, that their forces would kill us. There were groups, so we had to withdraw to Bratunac for our safety and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now prior to moving to Bratunac, were you involve in the Territorial Defence, the TO?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was that part of the Serbian TO versus the Muslim TO?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you move to Srebrenica -- I mean to Bratunac, had the Bratunac Brigade been formed?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you move to Bratunac, did you become a member of the Territorial Defence in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I received an invitation to go and work in the lead and zinc mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, who extended that invitation?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The company director.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So during that period, you were not mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when the Bratunac Brigade -- did you ever become a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when that was.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, since the Bratunac Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that would have been, what year at least, perhaps the month?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I think it was 1993, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what position you held when you were initially -- when you initially became a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: An ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm hearing some noises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me fast-forward to 1995, July. Were you still a member of the Bratunac Brigade then?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what your position was back in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I was at the APC at Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's also referred to as a transporter?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was your position, your particular position within the APC unit or whatever you want to call it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: For a time, I was a member of the crew. When the komandir of the transporter was demobilised, I became the komandir myself. I replaced him as komandir of the APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In 1995, did you hold that position, that is, being the komandir?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us for how long you had been the komandir?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how many members were you the komandir of?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Eight men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, that was the entire unit for the APC?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How many men per shift?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, this APC unit, did it belong to a particular company within a particular battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, all the companies wanted for security purposes to belong to someone, and they would appropriate us, if I could put it that way. And at one of the meetings of the commanding offices of the company, it was agreed that the APC came under orders of the battalion commander exclusively, otherwise we were listed in the second, or rather third company of the 3rd Battalion for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of that, who was your commanding officer, your immediate commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: At the time it was Dragan Zekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was the commander of the 3rd Battalion, right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that this APC was located in Pribicevac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us for how long it had been located there.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. When I arrived at Pribicevac, when I was deployed there, I found it there at Pribicevac located there from the 3rd of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And had it moved its location from the time that you had arrived there on the 3rd of August 1993 to, say, July 6th 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before we speak about the condition of the APC, could you please tell us where you and the other members of this unit would stay when you were up in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: We would stay in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where was the trench in relation to the APC; that is, the trench that was used for your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, at a distance of 3 or 4 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us a little bit what this trench looked like. Its dimensions, what it had, the amenities.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The trench was perhaps 4 by 3 in dimension. It was dug into the ground. There were some pallets for sleeping on, set up temporarily where we could put our equipment, and that's all. And an area for equipment. Our personal belongings, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now Pribicevac, as I understand it, it's sort of a wide area. During that period of time, from August 3rd 1993 to July 6th 1995, did you move the APC around Pribicevac at all?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, except in March, I think it was, 1995, when we were moved from the elevation point we were at in 1993 to be closer to the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What about your trench? Did you move your trench?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you hold that same trench when you were -- back in July 6th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we've heard testimony here that there was a place called Kula up there in Pribicevac. Are you aware of that location?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how far or how close your trench and the APC were located from Kula?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Until March 1995, we were located at Kula. When we moved it closer to the battalion command, we were about 400 to 500 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how close were you to the battalion command?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Between three and four hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say "battalion command," are we referring to the battalion command of the 3rd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the condition was of the APC.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was -- well, as a mechanical engineering man myself, the APC from the first day it arrived, it was out of order as far as I was concerned. And for the following reasons; it had the following things wrong with it: The systems connection on the APC was out of order, it never functioned at all. So the protective helmets, the interphone, and things like that. So the crew could not make themselves understood and communicate. The motor of the APC itself, the engine, in a short period of time would become very heated and expulse water from the cooling systems, so that was no use. Then the next fault was the planetary system for guidance was -- became overheated for steering, although the driver worked with the APC before, so it was easier for him. But there were fewer things that were right on the transporter rather than enumerating the faults that it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about the weaponry that was attached to this transporter, this APC?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Of the weaponry on the transporter, only the Browning was in working order. There were two guns which were out of order. The things used to launch the projectiles were out of order, but we didn't really need to launch any grenades from these guns. We would have to use a rope because the hauling wires were out of order. And then we would have to pull the trigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, of all the firing mechanisms, it was the Browning that worked?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us, what is this weapon?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: This is an anti-aircraft machine-gun, 27 millimetres in calibre, and it was mounted on a platform on the transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have ammunition for this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, from August 3rd 1993 to, say, July 6th, 1995, could you please tell us how many times this APC was engaged in battle activities.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Not once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how often you would fire the Browning.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: For Serbian Orthodox holidays, for Christmas, the Serbian New Year, Easter, there would be fireworks, a few bullets would be fired into the air because every fifth bullet on the browning was a tracer bullet and this was used to create a festive atmosphere. We never actually fired into Srebrenica, into the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you ever given during that period of time, from 1993 to 1995, and we'll stop with, say, July 6th, 1995, were you ever given any orders to fire the Browning at any particular targets in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you fire the Browning or the other mechanisms with the rope on your own accord?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Because there was an order issued by the Main Staff, the General Staff that not a single bullet was to be fired on the protected area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so in light of that, in light of that order, were you ever given any orders to fire, you, yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now I want to go to July 6th and move day by day onwards. And just as a point of reference, July 11th is the day that Srebrenica fell, and July 6th is the day when the activity surrounding Srebrenica began. First of all, let me ask you, prior to July 6th, did you receive any information or any orders to conduct any preparatory work concerning the events that were about to begin in and around Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever informed that there was going to be some sort of activities going on?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, up in Pribicevac, we've heard testimony that the Drina Corps established its forward command post. While you were up there, did you ever see General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know him by sight?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know him personally? In other words, had you --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic? And I'm speaking prior to July 6th up there.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: While you were up there, from July 6th, say, to July 11th, did you see General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about Colonel Blagojevic? Did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, are you certain you didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I'm absolutely certain, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us about what time or when, what date, if you recall now, that you saw General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I think between the 8th and the 10th of July, in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: But I don't know the exact date. It was in those days that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us where it was that you saw him.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw him at the so-called Do meadow above the transporter, some hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: He was observing in the direction of Bojna, standing there on that plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you go up to him to speak with him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was no need for me to address him, and had there been any need for me to talk to him, he would have sent his courier to fetch someone from the transporter. He was a very high-ranking soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you saw him, how close was he in relation to the command post, the battalion command post?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: About 400 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the command post itself?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The headquarters of the battalion command, the house where the battalion command was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we get into the actual details, a couple of minor points. During that period when you were up there, I take it you to eat. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would you prepare the food at your trench?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where would the food be prepared?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: It was prepared in the neighbouring house, next to the battalion command. We had a kitchen and a bakery for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- and would your crew, you and your crew, go there to eat?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it the food was brought to your trench.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, one person from the trench would always go with a can and bring back the food. Well, depending on how many people were in the trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you, yourself, went there to pick up the food from the 6th to the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on any of those trips, did you see your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During that period that you were there, did you ever go from your spot, your location where the APC was, to Kula, some three or four hundred metres --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever move the APC around at all to try to get it positioned --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I told you that the vehicle was out of order, and also we were not given any specific tasks to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did there come a point in time when you did, in fact, contact General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why you had this contact with him, and perhaps when it was.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: This was, I think, around the 8th or the 9th of July. On the meadows in front of the transporter, the village of Cicevci, the hamlet of Bejino Selo, as it was called, there I noticed troops moving towards our lines held by the 3rd Battalion. It was then that I approached the General Krstic and asked him what we should do next because we felt that as there were no units of ours in the direction of Srebrenica, I asked whether we should cover the area with the Browning, the area where we had noticed those troops moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say cover the area, what do you mean by that? Just point it in that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In order to stop the advance of the Muslim units to our positions, towards our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But my specific question is you said you wanted to cover that area. Were you suggesting to General Krstic that you relocate or reposition the APC or were you suggesting that you actually fire it? Which of the two, or if there's another possibility, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: It was not necessary to relocate the transporter. I was asking for further instructions with regard to opening fire from the Browning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was General Krstic's response?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: That we should follow or monitor the situation, that we should not open fire because there was no communications system that we could establish with the line where this was happening, and the reason was that we didn't want to injure our own soldiers, the Serbian men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you ever -- did the situation change where an order was eventually given to you to open up fire, to provide that --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why you went to General Krstic, why didn't you just act on your own, use your own judgement; after all you were the komandir of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would have the right to make a judgement on my own if there had not been any higher ranking military person there. Then I could have made a judgement on my own. But in view of the fact that General Krstic was in the vicinity it was my duty to seek further instructions from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why didn't you make any efforts to try to locate either your immediate commander, that is, Zekic, or Colonel Blagojevic, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of Mr. Zekic, I didn't know where it was. And as I said, we didn't have any communications system on the transporter or in the trench. So I was unable to contact Mr. Zekic. As for Mr. Blagojevic, as I've already said, I never saw him on Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, that was -- you told us you weren't quite sure of the date. Let me walk you through the days until we get to the 11th and tell us whether you did anything unusual or anything at all. On the 6th, did you do anything --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the 7th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the same applies to the 7th. We didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the 8th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The 9th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The 10th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th, well, I've just said. Either on the 9th or the 10th I had that contact with General Krstic. But nothing significant happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On the 11th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The same thing on the 11th. There was no movement of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did that APC ever move its position?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us to the best of your recollection the date when that APC was moved and the reasons why it moved.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, we moved that transporter for the first time on the 12th of July 1995. And we moved it in the afternoon when General Mladic arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you expecting General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Truth to tell, I wasn't expecting him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, tell us a little bit about this situation when General Mladic came. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: We were in our trench by the transporter. When General Mladic arrived, he asked us what we were doing there. We couldn't tell him what our specific tasks were because we didn't have any. We told him we were there, that we didn't know where to go. He said "well, the rear is being packed up, the kitchen, it's going towards Bratunac." He told us to move towards Srebrenica and to find our unit. To this I replied that we didn't have fuel in the transporter, not enough to reach Srebrenica. Then General Mladic called the rear komandir and asked him if he had any petroleum, and this man said yes. And then for the first time, I say for the first time since August 1993, they gave us 80 litres of diesel fuel for the transporter. When the fuel was put into the APC, we set off towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, had you -- you indicated this was July 12th. We've heard testimony, and it's pretty certain by this point that July 11th Srebrenica had fallen. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Since Srebrenica had fallen, why didn't you move your position?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Because I was waiting for orders from higher ranking officers. The battalion commander or somebody higher up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you go to Srebrenica as ordered?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us the route that you took. Later on we will go through a map. But first, if you could tell us what route did you take?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: From Pribicevac, there is a macadamised road leading to Zelani Jadar through a wooded area known as Sibovi, and we arrived at Bukova Glava, which is a hamlet of the village of Cicevci. From there, we went to the hill of Javor. That's a meadow overlooking Srebrenica. From Javor, we went on in the direction of the village of Biljeg, where there was an UNPROFOR checkpoint. From Biljeg, we went down to a place called Kozlje, and on to the asphalt road linking Srebrenica and Skela. And along that asphalt road, we reached Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you actually go through Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how far did you go through?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The whole of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, just so we know, when you enter Srebrenica, is that the entrance if you are coming from Potocari heading towards Srebrenica, or would that be from the other direction?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: From the other direction, from the direction of Zelani Jadar and Skela. When I say we passed through the whole of Srebrenica, we were moving in the direction of Bratunac. That's what I mean when I say we passed through the whole of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when doing so, would you have to go through the town itself on the asphalt road as you go through?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because there are only two streets in Srebrenica. You couldn't go down a third street because it didn't exist. So we passed through the town itself, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please describe who you saw in Srebrenica when you were passing through.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Srebrenica in the afternoon. In Srebrenica, I didn't see either Serbs or Muslims. I didn't see any inhabitants. It was deserted. There was no one we saw or came across.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: We didn't stay at all. We just passed through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You didn't park the APC to maybe visit your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us about what time it was when you arrived in Srebrenica and you were going through it, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was maybe 17 or 1800 hours in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us, from there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: On the road to Srebrenica, we had another breakdown of the transporter. Apart from all the other things I mentioned that were out of order, our caterpillar track wheel broke. We couldn't replace it. The caterpillar wheel would often come off, not to mention having to add water to the engine. So we continued on to the car repair shop called Vihor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now Vihor is in Bratunac, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us the route that you took once you left Srebrenica to get to Bratunac. What route did you take?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I'll be happy to tell you. Coming out of Srebrenica from the direction of Jadar, there is a football stadium belonging to the Guber football club. When we arrived there, there were soldiers there, and they told us that General Mladic had forbidden any military or soldiers from entering Potocari. Then we took a circuitous route towards the Sase mine, the so-called zero, that's the crossroads where the town cemetery is, via Zalazje, Gradina, that's the iron and zinc mine, and Bjlovac, and so we arrived at the Vihor garage in Bratunac. And it was night. It was sometime around 2300 hours because we couldn't move fast because of all the things that were wrong with the transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the soldiers that had told you that General Mladic had given orders that no one was to go to Potocari from that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were from the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: They weren't from the Bratunac Brigade because the Bratunac Brigade was relatively small. And we all knew each other more or less. Not all of us but over half. I would recognise over half of them. And I believe they were not from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to -- when you got to Vihor, what did you do? That is, in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As it was night, we weren't able to leave the vehicle in the repair shop, so we drove it to the centre of Bratunac where there were some logistics storehouses with logistics equipment or I don't know, quartermaster goods or something like that. But there were some guards looking after the warehouse, so we stayed until the early hours of the morning in the warehouse by the health centre in Bratunac together with the guards there who were on duty. We slept through the night. And when we parted, we agreed that the driver, as he drove the APC, should drive it off to Vihor to be repaired there and to report it, to report the faults that had occurred on the APC. And that's what he did in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me stop you here for one second. This place where you say there was some sort of a logistics location, I take it that was for the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where that is located.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In the centre of Bratunac by the health centre. It's an old building. It used to be a warehouse, but I don't know what it stored.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is that where one would also pick up petrol?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if that was the 12th of July, could you please tell us... If that was the 12th of July, could you please tell us what you did on the 13th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, the driver, as I've already said, drove the APC off to Vihor, and he probably left his telephone number where he could be contacted once the vehicle had been repaired. At around noon, at around 12.00 - well, I don't know the exact time, but anyway, thereabouts - allegedly, and I put this in quotation marks, they allegedly repaired the vehicle, but all they actually did was to replace the main wheel on the transporter and added some more fuel into the connection system. So into the gears. So they said that the vehicle had been repaired and that they could come and pick it up. Once the vehicle had been picked up, I don't know who the driver contacted, but he called us up individually, the members of the APC crew, and told us that the APC was ready and that we should be ready, too, to come back to the place we had left it the night before and to set off from there, once again, for Srebrenica, to join our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me stop you here. Could you please tell us --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who had given this order or instruction for you and the crew to head back to Srebrenica, if you know.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The driver, and he had ordered -- he had received orders from someone who said was the chief. Now, who that was, who represented himself as being the chief or head, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Didn't you ask him concretely who the person was?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And he said "the boss." Now, who the boss was, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you at that point contact your commander, your immediate commander Zekic, to see whether he had been the one --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there a reason why you didn't contact him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I've already stressed, the communications system on the APC was never operational. We didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What about commander -- Colonel Blagojevic. Since you were in Bratunac, a short walk from Vihor to the command post, right, did you go there, track down -- to try to track down Colonel Blagojevic to see whether it had been him and perhaps get even more complete orders other than to just go to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there a reason why you didn't make that effort, sir, since you were, after all, the komandir of this unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't go into the command, into the headquarters. And I think that the repair shop and the people in charge of repairing the military vehicles contacted the offices and the command once the vehicle had been repaired. It was their duty to inform the command that the vehicle had been repaired. So I didn't check that out myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But -- all right. Let me just get back to my question because I just want to make sure that we cover this point. I'm not asking whether you went to the command; I'm asking you why you didn't go to the command. Why didn't you take -- make that effort to speak with, or at least make an attempt to, to speak with Colonel Blagojevic to get concrete instructions since, after all, you couldn't reach Zekic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought that the person who said to the driver he had received orders from the boss, that it was one of the officers on the command staff of the Bratunac Brigade. So that was the reason I didn't go up there myself to check this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you carry out this order that had been passed on to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, if you recall, about what time it would have been that you set off toward Srebrenica from Bratunac on that particular day, that is, July 13th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly what the time was. I do know that we passed through during the day. Might have been 12.00, 1.00, during the day. But I don't know the exact time when we passed through Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us where you ultimately ended up on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We ended up at Bojna, above Srebrenica. It's a small hill and a valley. And we found our 3rd Battalion up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is that the location that you had been told to go to?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if you recall about what time you would have reached that location.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it might have been around 6.00, 1800 hours, 1900 hours, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what route you took from Bratunac to go to that area.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: We went via Potocari. There was no other place directly into Srebrenica, along the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why it is that you chose to go through that route particularly in light of what you had learned the day before; that is, coming from the opposite direction, that you were not to go through Potocari pursuant to General Mladic's orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that the driver, the person who said he was the boss said that the road was free through Potocari, that you could pass through it, and that we shouldn't go to Sase because it would require much more fuel because it's three times as long, that route, than it's via Potocari and there was free passage that way. And we didn't know what was going on in Potocari at all. We thought that the road was pass -- that there was free passage through the whole line.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Karnavas, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have about five minutes left before our break, and perhaps we could show you this map, what has been marked for identification purposes as D153.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I will walk you through this map -- or you're going to walk us through it, actually. And there's a pointer there for you.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The monitor isn't working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Hopefully it will. Is it working now?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, that's rather unusual. Okay, now it's working, I'm told. Okay. Now, if we could get the map over just a little bit. All right, First of all -- right there. Do you recognise this document that has been marked for identification purposes as D153?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is this, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: It's a map which I drew and the road, the route we took on the 12th from Pribicevac to Bratunac. And the next part of the route, from Bratunac to Potocari to Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We're going to go step by step. First, do you see your signature on this?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And there is a date as well, is there not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could walk through the map, if you could just tell us: Where is Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We may need to move it up a little bit for those who are watching. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I believe there's an X there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the route that you took on July 12th, 1995, when you went from Pribicevac and you were heading to Srebrenica pursuant to General Mladic's orders.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as I've indicated with a cross here, I marked it with a cross, this is the Pribicevac elevation point. Then I said we took the route, this route. It is a macadamised road, Bukova Glava, Javor, an elevation point above the meadow. We didn't go down to Zelani Jadar, and I didn't indicate that either on the map. We went across the field or meadow, here, and then went down on to the asphalt road, Jadar-Srebrenica, and took that route as I have indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is the 1 that's located there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And from Srebrenica on the 12th, you said you went to Bratunac, to Vihor. What route did you take from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: We took this route, a road towards the zinc and lead mine towards Sase at the exit towards Srebrenica. We took the right fork of the road across Zalazje, Gradina, Biljaca, Bjlovac, Voljevica, and reached Bratunac. And that's the point that I have marked with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the following day, on July 13th, 1995, could you please show us the direction that you took, the route that you took, to go to the location in Srebrenica where you had been instructed once again to do so.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: So, we moved from Bratunac across Potocari, that's the shortest route, via Potocari, and reached our destination point here that I marked, number 3, Bojna. It is the hill above Srebrenica which is where we were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And just one last question before we take a break: Could you please tell us the difference in distance between the route that you took on the 12th from, say, Srebrenica to Bratunac, versus the route that you took on the 13th from Bratunac to Bojna, which is by Srebrenica. What's the distance difference if there is any?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see that. It's obvious. On the 12th, you can see that we covered two and a half times, a two and half time longer route from Pribicevac to Bratunac than on our return journey from Bratunac to Bojna. You can see that very easily here. You can calculate it. But I'm sure it's two and a half times longer, that route, compared to the route we took on the 12th, or rather the 13th, when we returned. Because look, Pribicevac goes this way, so this is shorter. Srebrenica-Bratunac, this way is much shorter than going round about taking that byroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just one last question: Is there a difference in the quality of the road?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you just briefly tell us what's the difference between the road that you took on the 12th versus the road that you took on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The road on the 12th, I'm just saying directly now from Srebrenica towards Bratunac, that road was a narrow road. The surface damaged quite a bit because underneath that road through Zalazje and Sase was where the pits were of the mine. And the road has sunk in certain places. Now, the road from Bratunac towards Srebrenica via Potocari is a much broader road, much wider, it's straighter. And without these pits and depressions, without this sunken -- these sunken parts. So that's the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And just for the record, the gentleman, again, was referring to what has been marked for identification purposes as D153, and he traced his route starting with the X, 1 being Srebrenica, 2 being Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 2 being Bratunac, that would be July 12th then, from 2 to 3 July 13th. Thank you. Perhaps this may be a good time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. We are on the 13th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us, when you got to that location which is marked on the map as 3, and I'm referring to D153 for identification, could you please tell us how long you were at that location.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: About 15 to 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During that 15- or 20-day period, did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Except to go home and have a bath. But the vehicle did not move.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you asked to search any terrain while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you a part of a video which has been admitted into evidence as P21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe we can see it. You can see it a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you see yourself anywhere in this video, in this frozen frame?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we could get a little bit closer, just an inch or two. All right. Who are you in the picture?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The one with the cigarette in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it to your -- as we are looking at this frame, the person to your right has a beard and a cap on. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could play a little bit more of this video, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could just back up a little bit, please. And I apologise to the technicians. Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in this frame of P21, we see what looks something like a tube. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: This is a gun barrel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, is that for the Browning?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is that for?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Those are the two guns I mentioned. One is on the right-hand side. The ones I said were out of order. These were artillery pieces on the transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The individuals, by the way, that we've seen on transporter, do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who they are.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: The one in the foreground now is Vidoje Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we see some -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go back --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The person with the cap is who?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: That's Ratko Zivanovic, also known as Kurjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about this gentleman with --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: This is Goran Zekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what about this individual? Is he with your unit as well, the one right at the bottom, right below Goran Zekic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: This photograph is unclear, but no, he's not. I cannot identify him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could stop just for a second. If we could move back just a little bit first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In front of Zekic, we see that there is a barrel. What is that from?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In front of Zekic is the Browning, the barrel of the Browning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recognise any other individuals by name?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I recognise the man next to the gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And is that the individual with the cigarette in his mouth?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is his name, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Dragoljub Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, were all these men with your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go a bit, if we could continue with the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We could stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could continue. If we could stop for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this vehicle here with the launchers on it, was that in front of you or is that behind you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Not in front of us. If it was behind us, I couldn't see it because of the Browning that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So did you notice it when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to read a passage from the Butler report and see if you could help us out here. And I'm referring to -- at this moment, the actual number is escaping me of this exhibit. But I'm referring to 5.21. It's on page 44 of his revised narrative of 1 November 2002. It states that, and I'll read it, it's a short passage. It says: "Analysis of the Petrovic video provides further evidence of Bratunac Brigade elements in Potocari on 13 July 1995. As buses were being loaded with Muslim women and children, a Serb, OT-60 armour personnel carrier is seen driving up and alongside the buses. The military registration (bort number) of this vehicle is 10864. According to Drina Corps technical service documents dated 23 August 1995, that vehicle was assigned to the command of the Bratunac Brigade." And there's a footnote there. And then it goes on: "The vehicle is filmed remaining in an area for approximately five minutes. And in one instance, an unidentified Muslim male is seen talking to a Serb soldier riding on top of the vehicle." And I just read from what has come into evidence as P358, paragraph 5.22, page 44 of the Butler report. My question, sir, is were you in Potocari on July 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you stay there for approximately five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us why you were there, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: As I stated previously, when the APC was partly repaired in Bratunac, we were instructed to pass through Potocari because of the length of the route compared to what was described in the previous report. That's why we were told to go through Potocari, and that's how we came to be in Potocari on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were stopped there for five minutes or so, could you please explain to us what the reason was. Why did you remain there for five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can explain it. The reason why we stopped was that on the asphalt road, or rather on the plateau in front of the Feros factory, there were many Muslims, women, children, elderly men, and also military-able men. And we had to stop to give them time to get out of the way, to get off the road surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: While you were there, sir, did you at any point in time order or allow your men to point any weapons at any of the Muslim civilians that were trying to get on to these buses?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. If any weapon had been pointed at them, as the camera shows, well, you wouldn't be able to see all of us peacefully smoking cigarettes. You can see that if you look carefully at the shot of me, you will see that the cigarette smoke is still hanging on -- the ash is still hanging on the cigarette, that it hasn't fallen off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you hang around there at all with your APC in order to try to intimidate any of these Muslim women and children and men who were trying to get on the buses at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether any of your men harassed any of those Muslim women, children, or men that were there as you were parked for that period of time, five minutes waiting for them to get by?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, because nobody left the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we know from Mr. Zekic, his statement to the OTP dated 29 November 2001 and from the photograph that has come into evidence as P22 where it features you smoking, that you were identified as early as 26 November 2001 by Mr. Eskic, and then by Zekic on 29 November 2001. We also know that the report, the revised report was prepared on November 1 2002. Could you please tell us whether during that period, that 12-month or 11-month period prior to Mr. Butler preparing his report, did anyone from the Office of the Prosecution ever visit you to ask you what, if anything, you were doing there on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, where have you been living all this time, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you move about openly, or are you in hiding so in the event the Office of the Prosecution -- in the event they wanted to, they were curious enough, interested enough, concerned enough to meet and speak with you, would they have been able to find you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: At any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as a result of this particular video that has been shown on television, has it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you yourself had any problems?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what those problems are.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was very unpleasant. When I come across my fellow citizens, Muslim returnees I grew up with or worked with in the same enterprise for 20 years, they no longer greet me. They ignore me. On every 10th or 11th day of the month, they visit their memorial centre and as they are passing by they point their fingers at me. The donor funds for the rebuilding of houses, well, I had two houses burnt down. My apartment was devastated. But I have not received a penny or a brick to rebuild my property and continue living normally. And I won't go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, when was the first time, other than on the 12th you told us you drove through Srebrenica, when was the first time you returned to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th, on the way back from Bratunac. And as early as on the 15th or 16th, I can't be precise as to the exact date, my wife returned. And from time to time, I went there to restore the water supply of Srebrenica. And she was cleaning out the apartment so that we could move back to our own apartment from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would have been July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the Prosecution has been asking various witnesses if they are aware that there were -- that according to UNMO reports, reports from the UN Military Observers, assuming that they are correct, whether there were rockets that were launched into the enclave on the 6th of July. Are you aware of any rocket launchers -- rockets being launched into Srebrenica from the position that you were?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Had any rockets been launched, there would be traces on the buildings in Srebrenica or on the asphalt and I would have observed these when I came back. I am still living in Srebrenica, but I have never found or come across any traces of these rockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to go step by step, because there's a series of questions the Prosecution tends to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the questions could just be asked without the preface that the Prosecution asked a certain type of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not asking them. They're asking them. They're relying on UNMO reports. I don't, I don't take -- believe that these reports are accurate. The Prosecution tends to believe that they're accurate. They're their questions, not mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may just quote that UNMO report, instead of mentioning the Prosecution to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I don't have what part of the report they're claiming that this came from because they just state, for instance, yesterday was: Are you aware that UNMO also reported that seven rockets were launched or were used by the Bosnian Serb Army of the 7th of July. These are their questions, so I'm asking them. I can ask just the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, just the question without mentioning anything said by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that I'm not claiming that this is accurate. That's why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. We understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the 7th of July? Are you aware if any rockets, seven rockets in particular, were launched or were used by the Bosnian Serb Army on that day? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware, according to the UN Military Observers again, that on the 10th of July, it was reported that eight rockets were fired in the direction of Srebrenica in the morning? From where you were located, did you observe that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I would certainly have observed them if they had been fired. But they were not fired from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then we're told that in the afternoon on the same day that rockets - again, according to the UN Military Observers - were launched into the town itself, into the town. Now, did you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you drove through the town on the 13th, did you see any evidence where rockets had hit the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you returned to Srebrenica, your wife returned and you had these visits and you were assisting in -- with the water supply, did you notice whether rockets had hit the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you've indicated that you have been living there --

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so since you have been living there, are you aware of any construction that has been done to repair any damage caused by rockets that had been fired into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it no one from the Office of the Prosecution has contacted you to you could probably give them a tour of Srebrenica where they can point out any damage done in Srebrenica as a result of these rocket attacks?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we've heard testimony yesterday that the rocket platoon of the Bratunac Brigade sent a vehicle up there to Pribicevac on the 10th of July. When you were there, did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where was it located when you noticed it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I was near the transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's the APC.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far was the APC to this truck with the launching equipment or whatever you want to call it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: About 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now assuming rockets had been launched from that vehicle, from the -- from your position where you were located, would you have been able to see it and maybe even hear it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. It's a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And did you see and hear any rockets being launched from that vehicle that had been sent from the rocket platoon of the Bratunac Brigade on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you a couple of other matters. First, I want to show you what has been -- what has come into evidence as D149. Could you please take a look at that, sir. Do you see it? Do you recognise it? Okay, now, just for the sake of going through this, it states here that it's dated July 3, 1995. And we can see this is a request for equipment and materiel. And at the bottom, we see the name of Dragoslav Trisic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, obviously you know Mr. Trisic?
