utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could look at the one column under number 1, and I believe -- well, under number 1, it says "ammunition." And if we go down this column, at least on the second item, it says: "12.7-millimetre bullets, Browning, 10.000." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are those the kind of bullets that your Browning takes?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were any issued to you on this particular day, 3 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why not? 10.000 were issued. How could -- how do you know that none of them came your way?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Because I didn't request a single bullet. We had enough ammunition. And we didn't open fire anywhere. So we didn't need any ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, under this column of ammunition, is there anything else that would be relevant to the APC that you had?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. Because we didn't request anything. We didn't require anything for the transporter, so nothing was relevant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me show you another document dated 12 July 1995, again from Mr. Trisic. And this has been admitted into evidence as D131. If you could please look at it. And for the sake of time, this is titled "consumption of materiel and equipment," and it's submitted to the Drina Corps. Do you see Mr. Trisic's name at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go down the list and we go to number 3, it says "bullets, 12.7-millimetre Browning." And here it says 2.850 pieces. So assuming this report is correct, it would appear that from the 10th to the 12th of July, 2.850 pieces or bullets of this calibre were consumed by the Bratunac Brigade. My question is, does this figure reflect the bullets that would have been consumed or had been consumed by your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I am claiming before this Honourable Chamber, I hold myself morally and criminally responsible, that not a single bullet was fired with that Browing, and I'm ready to stand trial if necessary for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That won't be necessary. But thank you. Now, sir, do you know Mr. Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I know him by sight, but I didn't have occasion to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How much contact did you have with Mr. Blagojevic during those days; that is, from July 6th to onwards, say, the end of July? How much contact did you have with him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you by any chance go off to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Is there a particular reason, sir, that you wanted to come and testify in this particular court?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what that reason is.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you. One of the most important reasons is that I wanted this Tribunal to know the truth about this transporter or APC which absolutely did not take part in any combat activities between the 3rd of August 1993 until the signing of the Dayton Accords. A second reason is the broadcasting, and I consider this an abuse of myself, the fact that I was shown on this APC because this resulted in a great deal of unpleasantness for me which I have described a moment ago. And that is why I wanted to come to this Tribunal, to show my face, and to tell the truth about this APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tanasijevic, for your very honest answers. And I would appreciate it if you would be as candid and honest with the Prosecution and with the Court, and perhaps even with Mr. Lukic, as you have been with me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross? Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, first, about this incident that you talked about on either the 8th or 9th or 9th or 10th of July involving some troops moving towards your lines. Now, you said that you spoke to General Krstic at that point because he was in the vicinity. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, you'd also explained that your commanding officer was the -- was Mr. Dragan Zekic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Is it possible that his first name is actually Dragomir and not Dragan?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Dragomir is his real name. But we called him Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. You also testify that he was your immediate commanding officer. He was the one, therefore, that you would receive orders from?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, the position where you were at, at about the time of that incident, was a position that you had been holding since March of 1995; is that correct, when you moved away from Kula?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you testify that you spoke to General Krstic, not your commanding officer, because you did not know where the headquarters of the battalion was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So at that time, you did not know where Major Zekic's headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Even though he was your immediate commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you now about the 12th of July 1995. But before I do that, I'd like to ask you maybe a couple preliminary questions here. From Pribicevac -- all right, let me start by this. You are from this area, as you explained to us, and you know the roads in that area well?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you. From Pribicevac to, let's say, to Bratunac, now, how long would it take to drive if you went through Jadar, Srebrenica, Potocari, up to Bratunac? How long would that take to drive if you're in, say, a Lada Niva?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me work out the number of kilometres it is. You would need perhaps an hour because there's some dirt road, macadam road. From Bratunac to Pribicevac, it would take about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And a Lada would be the type of vehicle that would handle dirt roads?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But these are roads leading through woods which are not very good going from Jadar to Pribicevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, from Pribicevac, there is also another way to Bratunac, not going through Jadar but going through Sase; is that correct? Going through Sase and Bjlovac on to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, again, in a Lada Niva, how long would it take to drive that route?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: A little less. Perhaps 20 minutes less than taking the other route because from Sase to Pribicevac, if you take that road, it has just been opened up, the road. Only the earth has been leveled, and there's quite a lot of macadam, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: My question is at the state of the roads, let's say, in July 1995, how long would it take to drive from Pribicevac to Bratunac going through Sase and Bjlovac and not going through Jadar, to be clear? If you can remember.

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Around an hour, as I said. More or less the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What -- do you recall what I mean it was that you first saw General Mladic as you say in Pribicevac on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: It may have been about 1.00 or 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you met him, did you -- before then or after, did you learn that he had arrived any time earlier than when you first saw him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard from the people in the rear when I went to fetch lunch that he was somewhere there, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when was that that you heard this? This was before you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Around the 8th or the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm just asking about the 12th of July. Did you hear on the 12th of July that he had arrived at some particular time before you saw him?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you actually see him pull up into Pribicevac in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: A military jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was he alone or was he with others?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: He had four escorts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was there anyone else, any other officers?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. On that occasion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your battalion is the 3rd Battalion. That was stationed in the Pribicevac area at the time of, let's say, the 10th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, are you aware that that battalion -- or soldiers from that battalion moved from that position?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No, because I was separated. I was in a separate position, so I didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you were not aware then that on the 11th of July, troops in that battalion moved down towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Were you given any orders on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you weren't given any orders even to protect Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive anything. But this was implied, the very fact that we were there meant that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, you saw the videotape which was Prosecution Exhibit P21. And you mentioned that you had -- you were there in that area for five minutes. Right? You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you see any men being separated from that group of people in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You did mention that you saw women, children, as well as men in that group. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It's the Prosecution's position that those men in that group were later executed. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: I heard later on, but I don't know anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just one final area here. Pribicevac is at an elevation compared to some of the areas around it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And Srebrenica is, of course, at a lower elevation. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And from Pribicevac, you can see Srebrenica from there; that's one of the reasons that's an important place for the military to hold. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You testify that there was an order from the Main Staff, the General Staff, that "not a single bullet was to be fired in the protected area of Srebrenica." Do you know if those orders were ever violated?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: From the APC, no. But as for the other lines, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you say "from the APC," you mean your own APC?

utterances.speaker: MILOMIR TANASIJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just, I believe it's D153, which is the map that was marked by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any objections? Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. This document D153 is admitted into the evidence. Are there any documents to tender on your part, Mr. Shin?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The usher will show you out of the room, and we wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't say anything at the time, but if -- I would appreciate it in questioning witnesses if counsel, we understand he's putting the Prosecution on trial and their investigation on trial, but in that regard there is no need to suggest to the witness that the Prosecution does not care about speaking to him or does not care about the issue. And there's also this implication that there is something else insidious against this man going on. That's just not necessary. It happens every day. And yes, we are getting used to it. But it is sowing discontent among the community, and it's really not necessary. As I think the Trial Chamber is aware, the evidence regarding this APC came in from Mr. Butler. This witness agreed with Mr. Butler. So I can understand that, all the reasons, and they were good reasons for Mr. Karnavas to put on this witness and other evidence, but to suggest that the Prosecutor to this witness doesn't care or is -- it's really not necessary. And as I say, I just wanted to bring that up at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I take exception to the Prosecution's contention that it's not necessary. One, because Butler -- it's in Butler's report; two, these people are available; three, they have had seven years to investigate this case. And if they're going to make assumptions that this APC was involved in any way, then at least they should duly investigate their case. And this man has suffered as a result of this video being played over and over and over again because the assumption is that he was there doing something nefarious. And if the Prosecution wanted to be fair with him, they could have made a public announcement that that APC had nothing to do in Potocari on July 13th other than going through. They never gave the man a fair chance. And I think I'm perfectly -- it's a perfectly legitimate question to say: If they wanted to meet with you, were you there or were you in hiding? Because we're able to find him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, if Mr. Karnavas -- no problem with him asking this witness if he was interviewed by the Prosecution or not. If he wants to take on the investigation, I have no problem with that. Telling a witness that the Prosecution doesn't care and implying like he just has that the Prosecution has some insidious motivation is sowing discontent. What Mr. Karnavas appears to be doing, and I don't know if he's doing it on purpose, but he's trying -- he is building up something that the Prosecution's case is not, and then knocking it down. Our evidence related to this APC came from Mr. Butler. Now, this evidence, if I would argue it, which I will briefly argue in response, shows that the Bratunac Brigade like Mr. Butler was there, what it had eyes and ears and it was present and that it was there and this vehicle and its guns were there and it was around the situation. This is the Prosecution's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, please do not go into the substance of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has accused me of suggesting this man is a war criminal. And this man will take that back to Bratunac with him and take his view of the ICTY. I don't know if this man is a war criminal. All I know he was in Potocari with this APC with its guns all around these people that were separated at the time and were murdered. And that's what we asked him about, and that's what he said. And the innuendo and the implication that we're calling him a war criminal is insulting and it's really unnecessary. And that's my point. Let's save the argument. But that's the point here. And this is going on and on and on, this kind of thing. And I just can't be quiet forever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this debate has been going on ever since the start of the Defence case, and we have spent much time on it, almost with every witness. But here, you know, I believe that the parties calling the witness to assist the Chamber to understand the situation there, but not to blame the other parties unless - unless - you've found very substantial violations of the Rules of Procedure. I hope in the future, both parties will bear that in mind in their direct- and cross-examinations. And if there's no absolute necessity, do not directly mention the other party at all because we have all the reports, we have all the evidence there. You might cite that report and do not disclose or speculate what's the case of the other party. Yes, since we still have about 17 minutes, could we have another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. He is ready. This will be our last witness for the week. Unfortunately, we were not able to bring anyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is it possible for us to finish this witness this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: May I ask you how long you'll take for the direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think it's -- in light of the modifications that I will make pursuant to the last order by the Court, I think about 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't think that they will take much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Karnavas, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Cvijetin Stevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: S-t-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stevic, where are you from?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where do you currently live?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, and currently, what do you do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I work in a transport company for passenger transportation as a reviser, an auditor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in 1992, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in which -- well, tell us when you were actually mobilised.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you had, sir, prior to that time, when you were a young man -- or I should say younger, you had served your JNA service?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were mobilised in 1992, could you please tell us what you were doing.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I was providing security around the health centre building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to fast-forward to 1995, and in particular the month of July 1995. Okay?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, in July of 1995, whether you were with the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in which unit you were serving.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In the 2nd Battalion, 2nd company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how long had you been in the 2nd Company of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Since March 1993, from March 1993 until the end. I was in that company until the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And the end would have been past July 1995?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where you were located during that period, that is, your company, the 2nd Company of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I was at the Zuti Most or yellow bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us for how long the 2nd Company of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade had been located at the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I found them there in March 1993. They were there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From March 1993 to July 1995, could you please tell us how much ground the 2nd Company of the 2nd Battalion had gained? How far had you advanced towards the enemy lines?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Not a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In front of us, we had the Dutch Battalion. They were about a hundred metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: While you were there, your company, do you know how often you would engage the Muslim forces or even the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: There was no engagement at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You were never ordered to attack the Muslim forces from there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the Dutch? Were you ever ordered, your company in particular, to attack the Dutch Battalion and maybe even to capture their positions?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to focus your attention to the period when the events around Srebrenica occurred. Okay?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm going to give you a couple of dates as reference points, the first being July 6th, which is undisputed as when the events occurred, and July 11th when Srebrenica fell. First of all, prior to July 6th, were you given any particular orders or instructions that events were about to commence concerning Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you, sir, at that point in time on the line?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When was it that you first learned that something was happening with respect to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, before the 11th, had you heard any fighting going on?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you hear any - any attacks going on from the 3rd Battalion or 1st Battalion, 4th --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you please tell us whether you did -- whether your company did anything on July 6th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about July 7th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about July 8th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about July 9th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about July 10th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: July 11th, surely that must have been -- something must have happened.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We didn't go anywhere from our trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. During that period of time, did you go home at least, see the family, take a rest?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On the 11th, did you learn that Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I saw troops passing by in the direction of Srebrenica. But I didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Where were they coming from and where were they heading towards?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: They were going towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So they would have been coming from the direction of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recognise those troops?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did any of them come by the company to greet, maybe introduce themselves?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did anyone, if you recall, inform you what they were there for?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the 11th, how is it that you learned that Srebrenica had fallen?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Soldiers were coming back from the direction of Srebrenica, and they said that Srebrenica had fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, since Srebrenica had fallen, were you given any orders at that point in time to maybe leave your positions?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On July 11th, did you and your company leave your positions that you've held for the last couple of years, since you been with the --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what about the 12th? The next day, the day after Srebrenica has fallen, did you receive any orders on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We received orders to set out in the direction of Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we're going to get to the map at some point. But could you please tell us the distance from your locations where the 2nd Company was located to Budak. How many kilometres are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: About 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how would you get there from your position?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What is the road like?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: It's an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All the way up to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: A macadamised road, a dirt road for Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From your position, in which direction would you have to go to go to Budak, towards Bratunac or in the other direction towards Potocari and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And does that particular road take you all the way to Budak, or do you need to veer off anywhere?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We have to veer off.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On which side, the left side of the road heading towards Srebrenica, or the right side?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: The right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: To your recollection, at what point on the road do you veer off? How far do you have to go towards Srebrenica before you veer off to head towards Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Less than 2 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we know that Potocari is ahead, and we know that there's some industrial sites, buildings. Could you please tell us, to your recollection, about where you would be on that road so you can veer off on the right to head towards Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: From the generator factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which is --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: The Feros battery factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's usually referred to as the akumulator?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you recall about what time on the day did you receive instructions or orders to go to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Around noon. Around 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall from whom you received this order?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: From the squad leader, the komandir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And who -- to your understanding, who was your komandir at the time?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: The deputy company komandir was Zoran Cvjetinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you hear this order directly from him, or was the order passed from him to others, and that's when you heard of it?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: He told others, and then we set out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know from whom he had received that order?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you set off at some point to go to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We took the road, the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before setting off to go to Budak, what sort of preparations did you and the other men in the company make?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We received a cold meal, an uncooked meal, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. No bread?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just bread and cans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now were you told the purpose for going to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you were informed at that time the purpose was.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: To go to search the terrain in Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you told how long you would be in Budak searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we get to Budak, and before you describe to us how the terrain was searched to Budak, could you please tell us whether you went directly from your position where the 2nd Company of the 2nd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade had been located for the past couple of years, whether you went directly to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you stop anywhere on your way to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: My company turned off near the battery factory, and I went on with my friends to see whether there were any Bosniaks there that we knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm kind of lost in time. Do we continue at this point, Your Honour? I don't know -- or do we take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is this the right time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This would be a good time right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll take a break, and we'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Stevic, we left off where you said that you and your friends went to see whether there were any Bosniaks there that you knew. Could you please tell us where it was that you went as the rest of the company had turned up -- turned off towards Budak.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: You mean in the direction of Potocari, that's where they went.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But the company -- you indicated that the company went off, took the turn towards Budak, and you and your friends, some of your friends, went to see if there were any Bosniaks that you recognised. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where you went to see if you can recognise any of the Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Along the road toward Potocari, the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, how far did you go?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: For about 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I saw buses, trucks, and people standing round the buses and getting on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone while you were there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who it was that you recognised.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I recognised a driver, a colleague, Redzep Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: He had set out toward the bus, he and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you speak with the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what, if anything, he told you or what you told him?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I went to say hello. I asked him how he was. He said he was all right. And he said they were on their way to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you have any further exchanges with him?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No, because he was in a hurry to get on to the bus. So we just said hello, and he went to get on the bus. He said they were going to Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Have you seen the gentleman since?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, where does he live?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: He lives in Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is he still living in Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, how long were you in Potocari at that area, you and your friends?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Ten to fifteen minutes at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had anyone given you permission, or had ordered you to go there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why did you go there since you been given orders to go to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Out of curiosity to see whether I could meet any old friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And while you were there, did you at any point in time use your weapon, point it at anyone?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you instructed by anyone, either from the Bratunac Brigade or anyone else, to assist in guarding the Muslims as they were getting on the buses?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you do anything to terrorise them or to scare them to getting on the buses?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about your friends that were with you from the 2nd Company? Did you notice whether they in any way used any intimidating tactics such as the ones that I've suggested?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, after that 10- or 15-minute period, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We went toward Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You say "we." Who are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: My friends and I.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long did it take you timewise to get to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We arrived up there in about half an hour and met up with my company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, were they there at the time when you arrived in Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you inform your komandir, who was, I take it, the acting komandir at the time that you not gone straight to Budak but rather had gone to Potocari, out of curiosity?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you went to Budak, could you please describe the manner in which, the formation in which you went to Budak.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you indicated that you -- you had received orders to search the terrain as you would go to Budak. Did you search the terrain?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how, in what formation, you got to Budak, you and your friends.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: How can I describe it? The way sheep go when a shepherd is driving them along. That's how we went, all together in a group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you stay on the road or did you walk through the woods to search for anyone?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. We walked along the road throughout.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the way to Budak, did you come across any Muslims, Bosniaks?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us for how long you were at Budak.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We rested up a bit, 10 or 15 minutes perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Along the road to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us in which formation you went towards Pale.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In a group. All together, along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you go off the road to search the terrain in any way?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you locate anyone on the way to Pale?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you come across any dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you come across any abandoned weapons?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you got to Pale, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We didn't stay long.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. From there, did you continue on?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: From Pale, we set out up the slope to the left toward Gornji Potocari. And there, we were deployed into groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. How long did it take you to go from Pale to Gornji Potocari?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We didn't go down to Potocari. We stayed up on the hill. It took us about an hour, or half an hour to an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you see Potocari from that location?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What were you doing up there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Lying down.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you given any particular tasks to do, anything?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you search the terrain at least?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us for how long you were up there.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Two nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And during the two days that you were there and the two nights, did you come across any -- any Muslims?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you take any prisoners while you were there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies or abandoned weapons while you were up there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: After spending two nights there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We came back along the same road, to Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then what? Once you got there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you got back to Zuti Most, you said --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We went home. We went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall what your next task was; and if so, when it was?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Two or three days later, we were called up to go to Bacuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where that is located.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: That's above Gornji Potocari on the left-hand side in the direction of Srebrenica. It's a hill and a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And could you please tell us when you got there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We sat around the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say "sat around," did you search any part of that area?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you locate anyone or anything?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And again, how long were you in that area?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: For two days. My platoon, and then we went home for two days. And two days later, we went up there again. So we would spend two days there, and two days at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I somehow lost the date because we heard so many -- two days. Could you please, you know, ask a question about approximately which day it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. If I could, Your Honour, go with the map, so that way we could both use this as a reference point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me show you what has been marked for identification purposes as 154, D154. And it's a... Do you recognise this, sir?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Which sign?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at -- first, I just want you to tell us whether you identify this map. Do you recognise it, the map itself?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, there is a signature there, is there not?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And there's a date as well, or at least a month and the year. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We don't have a date, but when did you write this in and sign it? When did you sign your name to this document?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I signed it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would be the 13th.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to go step by step. First of all, and I believe you have marked it 1, 2, 3. The -- where you have marked the 1, could you please tell us what that location is.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would reflect the area where your company was located for those two years. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it was from this position that you left on July 12th.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us where you -- show us exactly where you went on July 12th on the map. If you could trace that with us.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: From Zuti Most, I went to Potocari, and then from there on to Budak, Pale, and then we stayed here on this slope behind Pale. That was our direction of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So number 3, where you are, where you have the number 3, that would be the place where you ended up on the 12th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us again how long were you at that location.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: For two nights.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So that would be the night of the 12th, the night of the 13th, so if my math serves me right --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- it would be the 14th that you left that location. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We left, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And from there, where did you go on July 14th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We returned back to Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was the same route?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, along the same route.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't recall whether I asked you. But on the way back, did you come across any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So -- and how long would it have taken you to return all the way back to Zuti Most and on to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Not long, because it's downhill, so it's easier to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us when you left again to take up your next position. How many days were you in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Two days. I was at home for two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would that be the 14th and the 15th, and then leaving off on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So then on the 16th, could you point, perhaps even mark, where you were sent to.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Potocari, Bacuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you circle that, please, sir, and put the number 4 there.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at that position?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: For two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So that would be perhaps on the 18th when you left that area?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: For two days to rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then so around the 20th or the 21st, you would have returned again to that position?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: After two days' rest at home, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and I think that's fine with this map. We won't need it any longer. Did you ever go to Zepa, sir?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you recall about what time you went to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether you went to Zepa when the commander of the Bratunac Brigade went there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether he left for Zepa before or after?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I think I would like to show you at this point in time the video that has come into evidence already. And it has been marked -- it's been admitted as P21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could stop and maybe go back a little bit. Okay. We could stop right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recognise yourself in this still?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who are you? If we could keep the -- thank you. If we could keep the video there for a second, who are you? Which one of them?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: The first one on the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it -- are you carrying any weapons that you can see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I am carrying a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about a rifle?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have a rifle, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that's on your shoulder. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what else are you carrying?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: A rucksack with my things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the next individual that's right beside you, do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Mladen Radic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the older gentleman who is holding his rifle like one of those pictures that we see of kids trying to run away from home, holding it in that fashion, do you recognise that individual?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who is that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Vuksic, Miladin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you said you gone with your friends, are these your friends that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could play just a little bit more. And we can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Stop right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This individual that we see right here, is he one of your friends or within the company, the 2nd Company --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with him or anybody else that looked -- that was there in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No. No. I don't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we -- in looking at the terrain, could you please tell us in which direction is the camera moving toward?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where would the Zuti Most be? Would it be in front of us or behind us in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, you would have walked in the direction that we see. Correct? You would have been coming in the opposite direction of where the video is heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could do this without the leading questions, particularly in this area, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we could go back to the video, and if we could play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we can move back, I'm going to ask a question that was previously asked of Mr. Vuksic with respect to the camera. I believe the Prosecution wanted to know where you guys were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In which direction are the buses heading?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where would the buses have been coming from, assuming they're going towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: They're going towards Bratunac, but they came from Bratunac, and that is where they made an about-turn, in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What's facing the -- these buses are facing towards Bratunac, so what's behind them?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I don't think I need any more of the video. Thank you very much. Now, just a couple of questions left, you indicated to us that you live in Bratunac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we know that you have been identified by the Office of the Prosecution in this photograph. My question is: Did anyone from the Office of the Prosecution ever come to see you, to see whether you could shed some light as to what, if anything, you were doing on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Had they come to visit you in Bratunac, would they have been able to find you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And had they located you, would you have been willing to provide them any information with respect to what you were doing on that particular day; that is, July 12, 1995?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But no one came to see you.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions. I want to thank you very much for being very honest with us, and I will appreciate if you could answer the Prosecution's questions as honest and as forthrightly as you have done with me. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Again, we don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You testify a little earlier that your commander, and I believe you said it was Mr. Zoran Cvjetinovic, had ordered you to search the terrain when you were leaving Zuti Most. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he said that we were going to search the terrain. However, we didn't do any searching, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: In any case, he told you that you would be searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did he tell you what you were searching for?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you ask him?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you what you would do if you came across any Muslims, armed or unarmed?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You identified in that video someone you identified as your friend, Mr. Miladin Radic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Radic has told the Office of the Prosecutor that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can we have an actual quote, Your Honour, and a page where this comes from. I think we've had this before, this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure you're familiar with our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My position is quite opposite --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It's not necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's no debate. Let Mr. Shin finish his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sure you're familiar with our position that it is not necessary for us to identify the exact quote as long as we have a good-faith basis for our questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And my position, Your Honour, has been and I demonstrated that the lack of good-faith basis from time to time. Whether it's from sloppiness or otherwise it matters not. And I even just showed recently Mr. Butler misquoting the record. So I would prefer the page and the line. Assuming that the gentleman has done his preparation, he should be able to give that to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as I said before, generally speaking, the cross-examination, the party who conducts the cross could put a question directly to the witness, and later on, if necessary, we need the specific quotations from the transcript and from the previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The problem with that, Your Honour, and I don't mean to debate it, is I just received their list. I don't have the statement with me. So I'm being asked after the hearing to go and check to see whether they do have a good-faith basis for characterising what another witness said. And I found myself that from time to time that they have made mistakes. And he can certainly tell me from what page and what line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As a principle, as I said, the cross-examination does not need this kind of practice. But in this instance, as you request specifically, Mr. Shin, could you please be kind enough to mention that page or number or whatever as an indicia to this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, I will, Mr. President. And I appreciate your understanding of our position on the specific request here. The particular page comes from the transcript of the interview with Mr. Miladin Radic on the 20th of June 2002. The page reference, a useful page reference would be the ERN number, which is L0077040. And it may be helpful at that point to begin from line 3 and maybe read down to the rest of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Stevic, I apologise for that -- I apologise for that. If we could return to the question, you identified on the video someone as Miladin Radic, you identified him as a friend of yours. You recall that, correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Mr. Radic has told the Office of the Prosecutor, they were ordered to search the terrain. If they found any prisoners, to hand them over to either the civilian or the military police in Potocari. Do you have anything to say about that?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No one said that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to Budak, if I could. And I'll need a map for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: While the usher is assisting us, I would just inform Your Honours this is a map that has been marked Prosecution Exhibit 861.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now Mr. Stevic, if you could please take a look at this map, it's a more detailed section of that map -- not that specific map you've seen before, but a more detailed section of part of that area. Do you have the map in front of you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you see Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you see Pecista?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And Dogazi?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Can you please using the pointer tell us where it was you met the rest of your company when you returned there.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: We met up with them somewhere -- here somewhere. Around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I please have you mark that perhaps -- any colour will do. Blue is fine. Actually, red would be better, since that is a rather blue map. Could you please draw a number 1 there and put a circle around where you met them.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not able to pinpoint the exact place, but it's somewhere there. Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you know that you were supposed to meet the rest of the company there?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When did you find that out? When did you find out that was where you were supposed to meet the rest of the company?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: When we set off.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you set off from Zuti Most, you mean?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. So you knew when you set off from Zuti Most that that was where you were going to meet the rest of your company. How many people were in your company, Mr. Stevic, approximately?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm not asking the exact number. If you could just tell me approximately.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: About -- up to 50. About 50 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: About 50 men. Now --

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you went to this place where you've marked with the number 1, was the rest of the company waiting for you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: They were sitting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you -- if you could please, could you describe with a little more detail where they were sitting, were they sitting on the road, on the side of the road? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: On the road. Next to the road. Alongside the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And there was about 50 people there, then, as I understand it, who were sitting there next to the road, just next to the road?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time it was that you got to Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was it -- was it in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Was it in the -- I'm sorry. I'll let you finish. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: After 1.00 p.m. 1.00 or after 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you know if it was later than 3.00?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you know how long those men had been sitting there waiting for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the characterisation. He never said they were waiting for them. He found them there, not that they were waiting for him to arrive as if, you know, they knew that he was gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so, Mr. Karnavas. Please look at the transcript of the testimony of this witness earlier, just a few lines above. You may proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, I could not understand the gist of your cross-examination on this point. Maybe you'll show us later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, I will at least attempt to show you later on. And I'll be completing this point relatively quickly in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could just seek Your Honours' indulgence for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Stevic, to return to my question, do you know how long those men had been sitting there waiting for you?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: When you got there, did you join them sitting down, or did they all get up immediately and start walking off?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: I sat down as well for a while, and then we got up and headed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And how long was it you were sitting there approximately?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Not long, five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Stevic, you're from Bratunac. And this map that you have there, you're familiar with that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, up to a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, you had explained to us that you had turned off the roads towards -- I'm sorry, that the other men had turn off the road towards Budak, and you mentioned a feature there. And there were three different ways of identifying this building or structure, and I just wanted to know if they were all the same. There was a -- you said there was a generator factory there. Is that correct, where the turnoff is?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you just look at that map that you have next to you and indicate with that pointer first where this generator factory is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Stevic, if it would be helpful, perhaps I could direct you to a road that you've already marked on Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- Exhibit D154. Yes, there's Budak. Now, you'll recall you marked a map already that's marked Defence Exhibit D154. And perhaps we could provide you with a copy of that map to orient yourself. As you study that map, I would ask you to look at the number -- well, I'll let you study that map first. If I direct you now to number 65 on this map, does that assist you in identifying, first of all, then where the turnoff to Budak is; and secondly, where that structure is that you've identified?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: This is where the factories are, the generator factory in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you see a -- do you see the turnoff to Budak that you previously marked on the other map?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just point to that.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The turnoff from the Zuti Most-Srebrenica road, you said you turned right to go towards Budak. If you can just mark where that Budak is.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: For Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's the turnoff? That's the road from Zuti Most leading towards Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Stevic, when we look at this map, it looks like there's two roads that turnoff the Zuti Most-Srebrenica road towards Budak. There's one near the 65. Do you see the number 65, just to the left of the number 65?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And if you look further down, going down on that road towards Srebrenica, there's another road -- there seems to be another road to the left of that word Pecista.

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there's that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you see that there are two roads that lead off the Zuti Most-Srebrenica road going towards Budak?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Which one did the rest of the company -- not you, the rest of the company take?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: The first road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where is this generator factory?

utterances.speaker: CVIJETIN STEVIC
utterances.text: Here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
